findings.title: GrafanaRuleListItem rendered in a .map() without a `key`
findings.body: The old `<GrafanaRuleLoader key={key} .../>` had a key. The replacement `<GrafanaRuleListItem .../>` in the `'grafana'` case does not. `key` is still destructured and passed in the `datasource` and default branches, so the omission looks accidental. React will warn about missing keys, and reconciliation is unstable when results are appended or filtered. The component holds state (delete modal, silence drawer, clone redirect), so that state can attach to the wrong row. Add `key={key}`.

findings.title: Pause and Delete menu items can never render in the ruler-less list view
findings.body: `canPause` and `canDelete` now include the Grafana Prom-rule ability. The items are still gated on `rulerRuleType.grafana.rule(rulerRule)` (Pause, line 123) and `canDelete && rulerRule` (Delete, line 165). The new list view (`GrafanaRuleListItem` → `RuleActionsButtons promRule={rule}`) passes no `rulerRule`, so these conditions are always false. Users cannot pause or delete Grafana rules from the list view, even though the permission checks pass. The new `GrafanaGroupLoader` test grants delete and update permissions and expects exactly 4 menu items (silence, copy link, duplicate, export), so it locks this regression in. Either make these actions work from the Prom rule, or do not compute and OR in abilities that can never be rendered.

findings.title: 'Silence notifications' menu item does nothing in the list view
findings.body: In the list view only `promRule` is supplied. The Silence menu item is shown based on the Prom-rule ability (`canSilence`), and clicking it calls `setShowSilenceDrawer(true)`. The drawer is rendered only when `rulerRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(rule) && showSilenceDrawer`, and `rule` is undefined here. The click therefore silently does nothing. `SilenceGrafanaRuleDrawer` still requires a `rulerRule`. The test only asserts that the item is present, never that clicking it opens the drawer.

findings.title: Prom-rule abilities treat Grafana recording rules differently from the ruler path
findings.body: `useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities` derives Pause, Restore, DeletePermanently and ModifyExport from `prometheusRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(rule)`. The ruler equivalent uses `rulerRuleType.grafana.rule(rule)`, which includes recording rules. The inline comment even says 'All GrafanaPromRuleDTO rules are Grafana-managed by definition', which is the semantics of `grafana.rule`. With the new code, Grafana recording rules lose Export (and Pause/Restore/DeletePermanently) wherever the Prom-based abilities are used. Only Silence should be restricted to alerting rules. The new function also has no unit tests covering recording rules.

findings.title: Federated-rule-group check dropped for the legacy CombinedRule abilities
findings.body: `useAllAlertRuleAbilities(rule: CombinedRule)` used to compute `isFederated = isFederatedRuleGroup(rule.group)`. It now delegates to `useAllRulerRuleAbilities`, which hard-codes `isFederated = false`. The `isFederatedRuleGroup` import was removed. Rules in Mimir federated rule groups are no longer treated as immutable. Edit, Delete and Pause (where applicable) can be offered in the legacy list and table views, which are used by `RulesTable`, `RuleActionsButtons` and others. This is a behavior regression outside the new list view, and a TODO is not a substitute for keeping the existing check.

findings.title: returnTo parameter dropped from the rule view link
findings.body: The removed `GrafanaRuleListItem` built the href with `createRelativeUrl('/alerting/grafana/${uid}/view', { returnTo: createReturnTo() })`. The new one omits `returnTo`. The rule view page can no longer send the user back to the list with their filter and pagination state. The PR is about removing ruler requests and does not mention this behavior change. Also, `operation` is no longer passed by any caller, and the redundant `rule && rule.type === PromRuleType.Alerting` re-check after the type guard is dead code.

findings.title: Stale comments still describe Ruler loading
findings.body: The component doc says it 'Loads an evaluation group from Prometheus and Ruler endpoints', and the `expectedRulesCount` doc refers to the 'Ruler response'. The component now only queries Prometheus. A similar leftover is in `prometheusGroupsGenerator.ts`, where the comment about preloading ruler rules and the `cacheAndRulerPreload` variable name remain after the ruler prefetch was removed. These are misleading for maintainers.
